intro: Two short books from ancient China have been read for more than 2,000 years. One is the Analects, the sayings of Confucius. The other is the Daodejing, the book connected with Laozi. This unit is about what these books are and how they came to us.

You will see how the Analects was gathered by students, and how the Daodejing fits into 81 short chapters. You will learn how books were written on bamboo and silk. You will meet the old copies archaeologists found in tombs.

By the end, you can explain what each book is, who tradition says made it, and what scholars think. You can read a passage number like Analects 15.23 or Daodejing chapter 8. You can compare the two books.
bigQuestion: What are the Analects and the Daodejing, and how did they reach readers today?

timeline.t: Confucius is born in Lu (traditional date)
Confucius dies; his students begin gathering his sayings (traditional date)
Parts of the Daodejing are buried on bamboo at Guodian
Silk copies of the Daodejing are buried at Mawangdui
Sima Qian writes the story of Laozi at the pass
China's exams are based on the Four Books
James Legge publishes the Analects in English
Legge publishes the Daodejing as The Tao Teh King
Archaeologists find the Mawangdui silk copies
Archaeologists find the Guodian bamboo strips

the Chinese name of the Analects; it means collected sayings
a short piece of a longer text
someone who passes something on to others
the Analects, Mencius, Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, studied together

the classic of the Way and its power; 81 short chapters connected with Laozi

test.q: Which book is a collection of Confucius's sayings?
test.why: The Analects gathers the sayings of Confucius.
The Daodejing has 81 chapters; the Analects has 20 books.

test.q: Who gathered the Analects, as tradition says?
test.why: Tradition says his students gathered his words.

test.q: What does 'the Master said' refer to in the Analects?
What is the Daodejing's famous first idea?
choices: The Way that can be spoken of is not the lasting Way
test.why: That is chapter 1. 'Learning is a joy' opens the Analects.

test.q: What were many early Chinese books written on?
test.why: Early books were often written on bamboo strips tied with cord.

test.q: Where were the oldest known copies of Daodejing chapters found?
test.why: The Guodian bamboo strips, from about 300 BCE, are the oldest known.

test.q: What is unusual about the Mawangdui silk copies?
test.why: They put the De part before the Dao part.
Zhu Xi grouped them in the 1100s.

test.q: When did China's government exams end?
Who translated both the Analects and the Daodejing into English in the 1800s?
test.why: Legge published the Analects in 1861 and the Daodejing in 1891.

test.q: What do many scholars think about the Daodejing's author?
choices: It gathers sayings from several teachers over time
test.why: Many scholars think it took shape over time; tradition names Laozi.

test.q: What does Analects 7.1 show about Confucius?
choices: He saw himself as passing on old wisdom
test.why: He called himself a transmitter, not a maker.

choices: A book of words saying the Way cannot be fully put in words
test.why: Daodejing chapter 1 is a famous paradox.

write.prompt: Compare the two books. How is the Analects different from the Daodejing in how it was made and how it teaches? Use two or three passages, such as Analects 1.1, Analects 7.1 and Daodejing chapter 1 or 64 (Legge's translations), and say what readers have made of them.
tips: Name the book and the passage number each time.
Say 'tradition says' or 'scholars think' when you tell who made a book.
Compare the two books; do not judge which is better.
Use unit words like passage, paradox and version.
